一手握住其中一個球，另一球繞手快速左右擺動，使兩球相撞發出敲擊聲，同時產生搖奏聲: Hold one of the balls in one hand and swing the other rapidly to and fro around the hand, so that the two balls collide and make a striking sound while also producing a shaking sound. For a start, choose an instrument that fits your palm, then practise catching the swinging ball; once that is secure you can hold one in each hand and play in different time signatures.
來源未列出具體曲目或固定編制，僅顯示阿薩拉託作為小型搖奏敲奏體鳴樂器，用於節奏伴: The source lists no specific pieces or fixed scoring; it shows only that the asalato is a small shaken and struck idiophone used for rhythmic accompaniment. The player holds one ball in one hand and swings the other around the hand to strike it, producing a shaking sound and a striking sound; a skilled player holds one in each hand and can sound different time signatures at once, building a multilayer rhythm. An online demonstration shows it also being used to fill in the music.

阿薩拉託屬卡沙卡一類，起源於西非。其後在不同國家以不同名稱出現，如日本稱帕蒂卡、: The asalato belongs to the kashaka type and comes from West Africa. It later appeared under different names in different countries, such as patica in Japan and koshika in the United States, and there are other names too, such as kesse kesse, cangotche and koshka. Traditionally it is made from fruit dried on the tree, collected by children and filled with the orange pebbles found in the iron-rich soil of the Sahel; on the West African coast pieces of shell are used instead. These differences in name and in filling reflect its spread across regions and its local adaptation.
阿薩拉託的器身由兩個空心葫蘆球構成，傳統取自樹上自然乾燥掉落的葫蘆。葫蘆內可裝豆: The body of the asalato is two hollow gourd balls, traditionally taken from gourds that have dried and fallen from the tree. The gourds may be filled with beans, or with the orange pebbles produced by the iron-rich soil of the Sahel; on the West African coast small pieces of shell are used instead. The two balls are joined by a thin cord, sometimes braided from strips of old cloth, its length adjusted to the size of the balls. A small wooden stick is pushed through the hole in each gourd to fix the end of the cord, and glue holds it, though the material of the glue is not stated. The materials of the remaining parts are not given in the source.
阿薩拉託的音色來自兩個空心葫蘆球相互撞擊，以及球內填充物搖動所產生的短促咔嗒聲與: The asalato's sound comes from the two hollow gourd balls knocking against each other, together with the short click and the shaker-like rattle made by the filling moving inside. The player holds one ball still in one hand and swings the other rapidly to and fro around the hand so that the two collide; the speed of the swing and the way the ball is caught change the density of the rhythm and the clarity of the strike. Unlike a single shaker, the cord joining the two balls gives it both a shaking and a striking action, and playing with both hands can set several time signatures going at once.
阿薩拉託（kashaka）是源自西非的11類小型體鳴樂器，由兩個裝有豆粒或小石子: The asalato (kashaka) is a class 11 small idiophone from West Africa, made of two hollow gourd balls filled with beans or small stones and joined by a short cord. The player holds one ball in one hand and swings the other rapidly around the hand so that the two collide, producing a rattle and a sharp knock. It has different names in different countries; a skilled player holds one in each hand and can play different time signatures at once, building a multilayer rhythm.
